corrections: Replaced fixed diffusion step, speed, compression and quality claims with model-, scheduler- and hardware-dependent boundaries.
Removed fixed LoRA/QLoRA memory figures, universal parameter ratios and data-count rules; clarified that activations and runtime configuration remain material.
Clarified that classic PPO-based RLHF is one alignment recipe, not a proven complete recipe for proprietary models, and removed universal reward-model thresholds and cost multipliers.
Separated theoretical raw-weight size from end-to-end quantized memory and latency; removed universal accuracy-loss percentages and hardware compatibility promises.
Corrected long-context complexity explanations, distinguished declared window size from usable retrieval quality, and removed fixed FlashAttention and prompt-compression gains.
Corrected speculative decoding mathematics for finite draft length and scoped distribution equivalence to the paper's acceptance and correction sampling algorithm.
Reframed PagedAttention and continuous batching benchmark results as workload-specific rather than universal utilization or throughput guarantees.
Clarified that constrained decoding provides syntax/schema conformance only for supported constraints and does not guarantee semantic truth, authorization or business validity.
Corrected SentencePiece as a toolkit supporting Unigram and BPE and removed tokenizer-independent character and number splitting rules.
Removed fixed ANN recall, latency and PQ-byte claims, and clarified that embedding dimension and domain specialization do not guarantee quality.
Clarified model-merging compatibility as parameter alignment and common-base requirements for delta methods, with mandatory downstream and safety evaluation.
Reviewed the remaining Transformer, KV cache, RAG, Agent, training, MoE, evaluation, multimodal, prompting, guardrail and reasoning pages and retained claims with explicit engineering boundaries.

relationSuggestions.reason: Token IDs are embedded into the sequence processed by Transformer attention.
Autoregressive inference caches the attention keys and values of prior tokens.
KV-cache allocation and scheduling are central concerns of LLM serving.
PagedAttention, continuous batching and optimized kernels compose a serving system.
Speculative decoding is one conditional inference-optimization technique.
Dense retrieval commonly uses embedding models, while RAG may also use lexical or hybrid retrieval.
Retrieved evidence consumes context and trades recall against noise and prefill cost.
Tool execution requires external authorization, validation, isolation and stopping controls.
Tool calls use structured model outputs, while the host remains responsible for execution.
Classic RLHF normally begins from a supervised fine-tuned policy.
Quantization trades memory/bandwidth against kernel support and measured task quality.
Safety controls require offline adversarial evaluation and online monitoring.
